holes.notes: Identified from the banguide: orange disc '1' and the white line running due SOUTH from beside the manor/clubhouse to a red flag. I registered the banguide (2000x2000 px, not georeferenced) to the world frame with a 5-point similarity fit matching OSM water-body centroids to blue blobs detected in the guide: world = 0.96006*px + (-774.26,-862.79), rotation 0.03 deg, residuals 0.5-1.4 m on all five ponds. Under that fit disc 1 lands at (-100,-756) and the flag-pole base at (-88,-494); as an independent check the 18th green's flag base lands 8 m from OSM green w296165902, so the registration is sound. Length 268 m along the centerline = par 4. GREEN: the bright irrigated blob at (-85,-486); the Esri image is EARLY SPRING, so irrigated greens/tees are vivid green while fairway and rough are dormant tan, which makes greens unmistakable but fairway edges soft. The green complex reads as a 45 m NW-SE strip (green + approach); I took the wide SE lobe as the putting surface (462 m2) and left the NW neck as approach. Two small white bunkers (21 and 40 m2) bite the NE side, verified against a known bunker signature beside the 18th/practice green. FAIRWAY is the coherent mown corridor from z=-682 (a big pale unmown heath/rough covers the first ~75 m from the tee) down to the green, bounded west by the pond and a pale rough band, east by a pale strip and a cart path; its edges are the least certain item. TEES placed on the short green irrigated ribbon running (-105,-765) to (-86,-737) under the banguide disc, the only vivid-green feature there. No fairway bunkers found; every other bright patch in the corridor proved to be dormant/bare turf or the cart path, not sand (Steel courses are usually better bunkered than this, so bunkers may be missing rather than absent). Water: OSM pond w539915586 (1161 m2) on the left flank.

Banguide disc '2' sits immediately beside the 1st green (disc centre -> world (-51,-504)); the drawn line runs south, straightens at x~-28, then bends right through the pond gap to a red flag whose pole base lands at (-96,-185). 336 m along the centerline = par 4. I extracted the guide's own white line pixel-by-pixel and converted it with the same 5-point water fit as hole 1; the line is straight south to z=-294 then curves west, so the hole is a gentle dogleg RIGHT around two ponds. GREEN: unmistakable vivid-green oval x -110..-83, z -199..-171 (449 m2 as fitted ellipse) with one white greenside bunker hugging its SE flank (45 m2, x -84..-77) - that bunker is the only sand I could confirm on the hole. FAIRWAY given as two rings: (a) the main landing area, whose mown mask (greenness>33) closes tightly at x -58..-3, z -392..-282 - the east edge is the OSM course boundary against ploughed farmland and the west edge is a conifer belt; (b) a narrow approach neck threading BETWEEN OSM ponds w539915585 (1235 m2, dark/silted) and w539915584 (2617 m2, part ice-covered) and then opening west to the green. Both ponds are hard in play on the second shot. TEES are the weakest item: the ground at the banguide disc is pale dormant rough, so I placed a back pad at the disc and a forward pad on the small vivid-green patch at (-30,-457) that lies exactly on the guide's line start. Note the 17th green sits at (-94,-298), just west of this fairway - I kept it out of the rings.

The clearest of the three. Banguide disc '3' sits just off the 2nd green and its white line runs 480 px due EAST along the north side of a long lake to a red flag at (399,-172) - exactly the 'runs east along a pond' hint. I traced the guide's line per-column and converted it with the 5-point water fit; 487 m along the centerline = par 5. GREEN: an unmistakable vivid-green blob east of the pond, mask area 800 m2, fitted as a 637 m2 ellipse centred (393,-170.5); TWO bright white bunkers, one short-left/front at (387,-195) 35 m2 and one right of the entrance at (394,-152) 49 m2 - these two are the reference sand signature I used to validate bunkers on the other holes. FAIRWAY ring 1 is the mown corridor that the spring imagery separates crisply: a ~40 m wide green band bounded by pale dormant rough, running x 90..312 with the north edge falling from z=-197 to z=-222; automatic mask (greenness>30) gave 7530 m2, my smoothed ring 9140 m2. Ring 2 is the approach that wraps the NORTH side of OSM pond w539915582 (3853 m2) to reach the green - the second shot must play round or over that pond. WATER: the long shallow lake w539915583 (12517 m2, silty pale margins) forms the entire left boundary of the hole; the pond by the green; and w539915584 sits left of the tee shot. TEES: the disc centre (-70,-134) falls on a conifer stand in the imagery, so I placed both pads in the open mown corridor immediately north of those trees at z~-158, which is where the guide's line emerges; that is the one item on this hole I would call approximate. Neither OSM green belongs to holes 1-3: w296165890 and w296165902 are both by the clubhouse and are the 18th/practice greens.

Banguide disc 4 sits immediately SW of green 3 and its white line runs ESE to a red flag at the far east edge of the property; registering the banguide to the world frame (similarity fit on five OSM water bodies, scale 0.9628 m/px, rotation 0.01 deg, residuals 1-11 m; verified independently against the OSM golf_course boundary, buildings and tracks, which all land correctly) puts the disc at world (333,-96) and the flag at (755,11). The satellite confirms both: four mown tee ovals at (331,-100), (359,-82), (390,-93), (442,-70) - the westernmost matching the disc - and a bright putting surface with two bunkers at (742,10). Length along the centerline is 426 m from the back tee, so this is the par 5 (a 426 m par 4 is implausible). Playing bearing ~105 deg (ESE). CAVEAT on the fairway: the Esri imagery is early-spring dormant, and continuous mown fairway (greenness index >=33 against rough at 24-30) only begins at x~525, i.e. about 200 m from the back tee; between the tees and there the ground reads as pale heath/dormant semi-rough with a large sandy waste wedge to the south around (330-440, -60..+35). I traced only the confidently-mown corridor, so the fairway ring starts at the landing zone rather than near the tee. Bunkers: two left-hand fairway bunkers at (612,-56) and (633,-43) guarding the inside of the gentle right-to-left line, plus a small pot left of the green (718,11) and a larger front-left bunker (728,26). The ploughed field north of z=-80 is OSM farmland way 552221920 (out of bounds), not water. The water listed is OSM pond 539915582 immediately north of the tee complex (its south shore is ~38 m from the back tee); it is really hole 3's greenside pond but it is the only water beside hole 4. A faint pale patch at (754-765, -5..0) behind the green may be a further bunker but merges with bare ground at the wood edge, so it was left out.

Banguide disc 5 sits ~45 m south of green 4 (world (747,62) after registration) and its line curves west then south-west to a red flag at world (403,214). The satellite confirms the green end exactly: a bright putting surface at (400,211), 365 m2, with a single pale bunker hard on its right (east) side at (415,204). Playing length along the centerline is 397 m from the back tee (straight tee-to-green 374 m), a long par 4 that doglegs left around the forest edge. The corridor is unambiguous - the mown band runs NE-SW with dense spruce forest tight down its whole south-east side and open dormant rough to the north-west; the fairway ring is cut from the greenness mask (>=33 vs 24-30 rough) and is 25-40 m wide. TEE CAVEAT: the three pads at (672,47), (708,52) and (740,54) are circular built platforms with a pale sand-capped surround rather than bright mown turf on this early-spring imagery, so their identification rests on their shape, their line, and the banguide disc landing 10 m from the easternmost one; the back tee is the eastern pad. As on hole 4, continuous mown fairway only starts about 175 m out (x~575), the intervening ground reading as dormant semi-rough. No sand was found along the fairway either in the satellite (sand scan over the whole corridor returned only the greenside bunker) or in the club's own summer banguide aerial, so this hole is traced with a single bunker. The large teardrop-shaped enclosure at (562-613, 68-100), ringed by a bank and filled with mottled scrub, sits on the right edge of the fairway - it is unmown heath/rough, not sand, and is excluded from both the fairway and the bunkers. No water anywhere near the hole.

NOTE ON DIRECTION: the brief suggested hole 6 turns back south-west, but the banguide is explicit the other way - disc 6 lies just SE of green 5, at world (382,281) after registration, and its white line runs NORTH-WEST to a red flag at world (248,185), i.e. play bears ~306 deg. The satellite confirms a small bright putting surface of 362 m2 centred (244,178) with two crisp pale bunkers, one short/front-left at (243,191) and one behind-left at (242,164); green 6 sits immediately NE of hole 7's tee, exactly as the banguide draws it. This is a straight one-shot hole of 167 m tee-to-green - a par 3, which is why the only mown ground I traced as 'fairway' is the approach apron of ~710 m2 running from the green's front out to (300,205); the rest of the line is dormant semi-rough. The tee end is two built platforms in a gap in the spruce, at (379,277) and (351,264); like hole 5's, they read pale/sand-capped rather than green on this early-spring imagery, but the banguide disc lands within 5 m of the larger (back) one and their oval built shapes are clear at z18. Forest presses in on the right/east of the whole hole; the ground left of the line at (270-300, 275-295) carries further pale scrapes that are heath rather than sand. No water on or beside the hole (the dark patch near (236,303) is a tree clump, not a pond). Registration for all three holes: banguide -> world by similarity fit x = 0.9628*px - 775.79, z = 0.9628*py - 861.02, from five OSM water-body centroids, residuals 1.3-11.5 m, cross-checked against the OSM course boundary, buildings and tracks; overlaying my traced centerlines back onto the banguide puts them on its drawn lines and my green rings on its red flags.

PAR 5, 439 m along the centerline. ID: banguide disc 7 sits in the central hub with discs 14/16 and greens 6/13/15; its drawn line sweeps SE then S, passes outside the 12th green, and ends at a red flag in a forest gap far to the south. I extracted the banguide's white route lines as pixel components and fitted a banguide->world affine on six OSM water-body bboxes: world_x=0.96185*px-777.01, world_z=0.96066*py-862.75 (residual RMS 3.4/2.8 m). That transform put the line's tee end at (250,240) and its green end at (405,599); the satellite corridor matches exactly. GREEN traced from z18 Esri (474 m2, centre 393,605) in a spruce-walled gap - independently 11 m from the banguide flag, consistent with the 3-5 m agreement measured on greens 8/9/12. FAIRWAY is the mown ribbon between the big tree clump on the west (x 246-318, z 314-402) and the spruce edge on the east; it begins ~z 288, so the tee shot carries ~80 m of dry heath. TEES: the imagery shows one distinct raised, smooth mown platform ~45x28 m spanning x 234-279, z 216-244 (immediately E of a small shed at x 220-237, z 241-258), exactly where the banguide's line starts; the two pads given are placed on it, but individual pad outlines are NOT resolvable at 0.30 m/px, so their size/split is inferred. BUNKERS: none could be confirmed. Every bright candidate along the corridor (382,280 / 404,347 / 379,471 / 381,441 / 359,492 / 405,607 / the 45x46 m pale patch at 276,290 / the long pale strip at x 455-470, z 430-570) resolved at z18 into dry bare turf, a bare gap between trees, scrub heath or a bare east-facing slope - no crisp bright core with a shadowed face like the confirmed bunkers on 8 and 9. The banguide aerial is too blurry here to arbitrate. For a Steel course this is almost certainly an imagery limitation rather than a bunkerless hole, so treat hole 7's bunkering as unsurveyed rather than absent. No water anywhere near this corridor (nearest OSM water is 400 m north).

PAR 4, 331 m. ID: banguide disc 8 is the isolated orange disc deep in the southern forest; its line curves WSW then bends S and ends at the red flag at the very bottom of the plan. Through the fitted affine that is tee (229,727) -> green (50,967); the satellite shows exactly that: a narrow tree-walled corridor running WSW off a ridge tip, opening into a long north-south clearing that necks down to a green ringed by spruce. GREEN traced from z18 (492 m2, centre 51.6,963) - only 3.3 m from the banguide line's own end point, the tightest independent check I have on the transform. FAIRWAY: the upper 100 m is the tan, drought-stressed tree corridor (perpendicular width 18-30 m, a machinery track running along it); from about z 780 the mown band hugs the EAST tree line - greenness peaks at x 65-85 there and falls off to the west, so the pale ground on the west side of the clearing (x < 40) is rough, not fairway, and is excluded. The banguide's drawn line bulges further west (to x 42 at z 893) than the real mown band; I followed the imagery. BUNKERS: two confirmed, both with a bright sand core and a shadowed face - a 64 m2 elongated fairway bunker at (59,821) sitting right on the line about 150 m out, and a 44 m2 greenside bunker at (37,956) short-left of the green. Candidates at (71,775), (205,741) and (188,748) were checked at z18 and are dry turf, discarded. TEES inferred at the NE tip of the clearing (the corridor's head, x 208-230, z 706-720); no pad outline is resolvable, direction of play WSW 248 deg. No water. Walk from green 7 to this tee is ~205 m through forest - long, but the banguide shows the same gap, so it is real.

PAR 3, 161 m playing due north (bearing 1 deg). ID: banguide disc 9 is the southernmost disc on the plan, sitting essentially on the club's OSM property boundary (world z 999 there); its line is a short, dead-straight vertical run north to a red flag. Through the fitted affine that is tee (9,938) -> green (16.5,785), and the satellite green traced independently at (13.2,781) is 3.9 m away, so the hole really is a short one - I checked that the drawn line is not a fragment truncated by the flag graphic (the white-line component runs continuously from the disc to the pole base). GREEN traced from z18: 405 m2, centre (13.2,781), sitting on a shelf with dense spruce hard against its left/west edge. BUNKER: one confirmed, 28 m2 at (18.8,790), front-right of the green with a clear shadowed face. FAIRWAY: CAUTION - this ring is the semi-mown strip between tee and green, not a true fairway. Greenness there runs 27-36 versus 36-44 on hole 8's fairway band and 20-24 on the tan rough further west, so the ground reads as first-cut/heath rather than mown fairway; a par 3 here plausibly has no fairway at all. Drop the ring if you would rather render heath. The strip is bounded west by the spruce edge (which closes to x ~-2 at z 860-900 and x ~5 below z 915) and east by hole 8's fairway. TEES inferred: nothing resolvable on the ground at (10,940) - it is partly in the forest's afternoon shadow - so the pads are placed on the banguide line start and 22 m in front of it. No water. Walk from green 8 (51.6,963) to this tee is 47 m; from this green to the 10th tee (about -54,647 off the same banguide fit) is ~150 m.

Identified from the banguide: disc 10 sits immediately SW of the 9th green (banguide flag 9 -> world (22,768), satellite green 9 at ~(15,777)), and its line runs NW to a red flag whose pole base converts to world (-378,543). The satellite has a bright emerald green there at (-374,544) (area 465 m2 at the greenness threshold calibrated on the two OSM greens near the clubhouse, where thr=40 reproduced OSM w296165890's 493 m2 as 507 m2) - so the green is confirmed to ~4 m. Banguide->world registration is a similarity fit on five OSM water polygons (w539915580/81/82/83/84/85/86), scale 0.9601 m/banguide-px, rotation +0.05 deg, residuals 0.3-1.0 m; it was independently confirmed by greens 10, 11, 12 and 14 all landing within ~5 m. TEE UNCERTAIN: the banguide places disc 10 at world (-60,803), which is dense forest in BOTH the satellite and the banguide's own aerial. There IS a real mown chute ~15-25 m wide running NNW from the 9th-hole open ground at (-40,830) up to (-95,742), where it meets the SE tip of the 10th corridor; I placed two tee pads in the widest part of that chute at (-56,820) and (-71,798). No distinct tee-pad outlines are resolvable there at 0.30 m/px, so the tee positions are the weakest part of this hole. The corridor itself is unambiguous - a broad mown swath through forest running NW from (-125,715) to the green, ~50-70 m of mown ground of which I traced the central ~35 m as fairway. LENGTH ~427 m along the centerline, so this reads as a (short) par 5 or a very long par 4. BUNKERS: only one candidate anywhere on the hole - a rounded pale scrape with a dark grassed lip at (-370,575), ~15x9 m, short/right of the green. Its luminance (121) is below the confirmed bunkers elsewhere (138-150 at the 9th, 11th and 12th greens), so it may be worn turf rather than sand; I included it because a greenside position is exactly right and the shape has a bunker's lip. Repeated high-zoom sweeps of the green complex (x -420..-320, z 480..615) and of the landing zone (x -340..-160, z 555..760) found no other sand. No water anywhere near this hole (nearest OSM water is the 11th's pond, 196 m off the line).

The best-constrained of my three. Banguide disc 11 converts to world (-305,506) and the satellite has TWO clear raised oval tee platforms there at (-300,507) and (-269,500), plus a third, less distinct mown pad at (-247,496) - the only place in this half of the course with that signature. The banguide line's far end (flagpole base) converts to (32,436) and the satellite green is at (30,432), 4 m away: a direct, independent confirmation of both the routing and the registration. Green area 513 m2 (greenness threshold calibrated against OSM green w296165890). The green's south edge is masked by tall conifers leaning north in the orthophoto, so the ring may be a few metres short on that side. Plays 68 deg ENE, ~344 m along the centerline - a par 4. The corridor runs along the NORTH edge of the big southern forest; the forest edge is the whole right-hand boundary and it is the feature that makes the hole. NOTE: the satellite's forest edge sits ~17 m north of where the banguide's (summer, different date) aerial puts it, so a straight tee-to-green line clips the trees; I bent the centerline north to follow the actual mown ground. One bunker: a 17x6 m ellipse at (23,418) with a shadowed south face, front-left of the green. No fairway bunkers found in repeated sweeps of x -230..-120. WATER: OSM way 539915586 (1212 m2) at (-213,425) - I used the OSM ring verbatim since it is surveyed. It sits 61 m left of the tee-shot line and ~120 m from the back tee, so it catches a pulled drive; it is 196 m from hole 10 and not near any other hole, so it belongs here.

Green is certain: the banguide's 12th flagpole base converts to (348,435) and the satellite has a vivid green at (346,430), with a crisp 10x9 m sand bunker immediately front-left at (326,437) (luminance 149-160, matching the confirmed bunkers at the 9th green). Green area 415 m2. Hole 13's disc sits 73 m west of it, which is the expected green-to-next-tee walk and corroborates the identification. TEE UNCERTAIN - this is the main caveat. The banguide's disc 12 converts to (9,493) and the line it draws emerges at (32,494); BOTH points are dense spruce forest in the satellite AND in the banguide's own aerial (checked at 8x with brightness boost - no clearing exists). The registration is not at fault: greens 10, 11, 12 and 14 all land within 5 m, so the banguide simply drew the tee end of this hole into the trees. The mown ground begins at x~76, and the only constructed feature at the corridor's west end is a raised, rimmed circular platform ~20x16 m centred (91,488), 83 m walk from the 11th green - I have taken that as the tee. Its turf reads dry/dormant (greenness 17) rather than the bright green of the 11th's tee pads (39), so it could conceivably be a worn knoll rather than a tee; no alternative candidate exists inside the forest. Consequence: my centerline measures ~269 m (a short par 4), whereas the banguide's own drawn polyline measures ~341 m from (32,494). If the real back tee is a chute cut into the trees that the imagery cannot show, the hole is ~340 m and my tee is a forward tee. ROUTING: plays ~96 deg east from the tee, squeezes SOUTH of a rocky, scrub-and-tree knoll occupying x 150..220, z 459..500 (the banguide line also passes south of it), then opens out and doglegs left/NE to the green. Fairway traced as the mown band between the southern forest and that knoll, ~25-40 m wide. No water anywhere on the hole (OSM has none and none is visible). Only the one greenside bunker was confirmed; two further pale patches at (293-319,443-448) and (374-387,463-472) inspected at high zoom turned out to be a worn track and dry rough, not sand.

Par 3, 154/154/103/103/103 m. Registration: the banguide aerial was fitted to the Esri z18 satellite by FFT cross-correlation of gradient images - a single sharp peak at 0.958 m per banguide pixel, 0 deg rotation, giving world = (-534 + (bx-250)*0.958, -622 + (by-250)*0.958). It reproduces five independently detected greens (11,12,13,14,15) to 2-5 m. HOLE ID: the '13' disc sits 74 m from the 12th green flag (banguide (348.7,433.7) vs satellite green at (343.3,435.6)), and its line runs NNW to a flagstaff base at world (206.2,285.1); the satellite putting surface there centres on (205.2,287.3), 2.3 m away. Traced tee-to-green 153.97 m against the card's 154 m (0.02%). The club's note 'korthal mot kiosken' (the halfway kiosk is at this green) is confirmed by a white-roofed building at (226,247) between this green and the 14th tee. TEES: the club says only two pads exist (vit+gul 154, bla+rod+orange 103); both are placed on the axis at those card distances, the back one landing on open ground at the pine-block edge as the disc does. Individual pad outlines are not resolvable in the spring imagery, so w/d are typical values - medium confidence on tees. BUNKERS: none. This is a measurement, not an omission - peak local brightness in a 60x70 m box around the green is L=148, against L=171-193 at bunkers verified on the 15th and 6th, and no pixel within 45 m of the centreline meets the sand signature (L>150, R~G, G-B>22). The brightest features near the green are the kiosk roof and a 4 m cart path running S from (197,290) to (203,318). FAIRWAY: the mown corridor read between the pine clump at (195-250, 380-445) and the wood edge at x~258; edges softer than the green's, medium confidence. WATER: none within 150 m.

Par 4, 355/316/316/257/196 m. HOLE ID: the '14' disc sits in the busy junction that also carries the 7th tee, the 13th green flag and the 16th tee; its line leaves WSW and terminates at a red flag whose pole base registers to world (-134.2,345.6). The satellite's bright-green putting surface there centres on (-134.2,346.9) - 1.3 m agreement, the best of any hole here. Straight tee-to-green 350.7 m, corridor path 356.9 m, against the card's 355 m (0.5%). Green 481 m2. TEES: four pads (vit 355, gul+bla 316, rod 257, orange 196), placed at those card distances along the corridor measured back from the green; angDeg is the local line of play, which swings 243->246 deg as the hole sags. Pads themselves are not resolvable here so w/d are typical. BUNKERS: none found, and I believe that. The club calls this one of the two holes 'ut over heden' with a tee shot that is 'diffust' - no framing - and no pixel within 45 m of the centreline meets the sand signature; max local brightness in an 80x70 m box round the green is L=135 against L=171-193 at verified bunkers on 15 and 6. The tempting 41x27 m pale patch at (-40,320) is bare heath, not sand: RGB (156,150,112) with soft diffuse edges vs (177,173,140) with crisp shadowed edges at real bunkers. FAIRWAY: this is the weakest part of the trace. The corridor shows only as a faint greenness band, sampled at x = 40/0/-40/-120 as z 304-332 / 332-364 / 348-364 / 320-352; the ring follows those centres, which sag ~25 m south of the straight tee-green line - the banguide's own drawn line sags the same way, so the bend is real, but the edges are reconstructed, medium confidence. WATER: the pond given is 78 m off the green's left edge (nearest point (-200.6,405.2)) - the only water within 150 m, included for the scene but not strictly in play. The imagery over this whole western half is visibly softer than over the 15th/6th greens, which is why confidence is medium.

Par 4, 381/350/324/273/273 m - index 2, the second-hardest. HOLE ID: the '15' disc marks the west (tee) end of the upper of the two long parallel lines through the middle of the property; the line runs ENE and ends at the marker that also carries the 16th tee, beside the green traced at (180.2,194.6), 544 m2. Tee-to-green 381.08 m against the card's 381 m (0.02%). The club's tip calls it 'spikrakt hal' (dead straight) with 'gott om utrymme', which is exactly what the imagery shows - the centreline is a single straight segment. INDEPENDENT CHECK: the rod/orange pad predicted purely from the card (273 m back from the green along the axis, i.e. (-77.0,284.2)) lands on a rectangular mown pad actually visible in the satellite at (-74..-62, 282..287) - that pad was found before the prediction was made, and it corroborates both the axis and the banguide-to-satellite registration. BUNKERS: two, both crisp and verified by colour - RGB (172,169,136) and (177,173,142), L=171-188, the same signature as the 6th green's bunkers 60 m away, against L=123 for dry field. One short-left of the green at (166.9,180.7), one right/short at (186.0,206.7). Rings are drawn ~15% outside the bright core to include the shaded lip, giving ~106 and ~74 m2. NOT a bunker: the 27x32 m pale, dark-flecked area at (188-215, 160-192) immediately NE of the green is a rock/waste knoll - dimmer than sand (RGB 157,153,117) with vegetation clumps inside. FAIRWAY: the corridor is a clear greenness band; sampled centres at x = 120/80/40/0/-40/-80/-120 fall within 8 m of the straight axis. Widths taper 22 m near the tee to 36 m through the landing area to 22 m at the front. The western (tee) third is the softest reading, where heath and mow line are hard to separate - medium confidence on those edges only. WATER: none in play; the nearest pond is 94 m behind-left of the back tee (traced under hole 14).

Identified from the banguide: disc 16 sits in the mown lobe at the SE end of the heathland and the line sweeps WNW then NW to a red flag. The banguide was georeferenced to the satellite with a north-up similarity fit (world_x = 0.95*bx - 773, world_z = 0.95*by - 858, ~0.95 m per guide pixel) tied to three unambiguous landmarks - the west pond's north tip, the east pond's east end and the 3rd green. Under that fit the guide's 16th flag lands at (-172.8,-64.4), 3 m from the satellite putting surface I traced at (-170.2,-64.1), so the identification is secure. Green traced by greenness threshold on z18 Esri imagery, 382 m2, elongated NNE-SSW. THREE greenside bunkers are unmistakable in the imagery: back-left (-186,-69), right (-156,-61) and front (-167,-44); a fourth compact bright blob at (-99,-27) on the right edge of the fairway reads as a fairway bunker (10x7 m) - slightly less certain because the ground NE of the corridor is naturally sandy heath. The hole plays as a curving 449 m par 5 / long par 4: the guide's drawn line bends steadily, so the centerline follows the curve rather than the 395 m straight. Fairway ring is the mown corridor; its NE edge is the sharp turf/heath boundary read off the imagery (from (-39,0) SE to (61,142) and on to (205,151)), its SW edge is offset ~35 m from the play line because there is no visible mowing edge on that side (open turf shared with hole 15). TEE POSITIONS ARE THE WEAK POINT: no crisp tee pad is resolvable at 0.3 m/px in the dry spring imagery, so both pads are placed in the mown lobe where the guide's disc and line-end fall (x 164-195, z 151-153); treat cx/cz as +/-15 m. No water anywhere in this corridor.
